digest.intro: Oil tankers burning, DHS identities exposed, and a CPU baked into a language model.

items.title: Three Oil Tankers Erupt in Flames Near the Strait of Hormuz
items.blurb: Sea mines hit tankers at one of the world's most critical energy chokepoints as an oil spill simultaneously reaches UAE beaches — the Iran conflict's economic pressure campaign has turned kinetic in a way that could move energy markets fast. Meanwhile, Israeli elections produced no clear winner: Netanyahu's bloc likely falls short of 61 seats, and Arab parties won an unprecedented 19 seats on surging Palestinian-citizen turnout, putting them in a position to help form a coalition for the first time.

items.title: U.S. Warns Gulf States of Post-Midterm Iran Escalation Window
items.blurb: Washington privately warned Gulf partners of a possible brief, intense resumption of operations against Iran after the November 3 midterms — a diplomatic signal that the pause is tactical, not terminal. Pentagon costs of the Iran war have already crossed $47 billion, and Zelensky separately opened the door to offering Russia security guarantees for the first time, suggesting multiple frozen conflicts are approaching inflection points simultaneously.

items.title: As U.S. Ties Fray, Europe Plans First Undersea Cable to Greenland — Bypassing America
items.blurb: The EU's Pan-Arctic Cable project would directly connect Europe to Greenland and extend onward to Canada, Japan, and South Korea without touching U.S. soil — a flagship infrastructure move that would have seemed commercially pointless five years ago. It's the physical internet literally routing around American political instability, and it comes right after a trilateral deal preserved Greenland's autonomous status while expanding U.S. military access — an uneasy arrangement that's clearly driving European contingency planning.

items.title: Qwenputer: A Working RISC-V CPU Compiled Into an LLM's Weights
items.blurb: Someone took a stock Qwen 3.5 4B model and compiled a full 32-bit RISC-V CPU into its weights, using the model's own Gated DeltaNet linear-RNN attention layers as exact, addressable RAM — no sandbox, no tool calls, no external runtime. It ran 18 million instructions error-free and executes C and MicroPython entirely within the model's forward pass, which means a transformer is now literally doing clock cycles. The follow-up research shows this architecture can also hide reasoning inside the RNN state in ways that defeat chain-of-thought monitoring — which is either fascinating or alarming depending on your afternoon.

items.title: Why Is This Fingerprinting Script Generating Bioweapon Synthesis Routes?
items.blurb: A security researcher crawling the web to catalog canvas fingerprinting scripts found something they didn't expect: an obfuscated script that, when reverse-engineered, was generating bioweapon synthesis instructions. The piece is a meticulous walk through the forensics — fingerprinting as a cover for dual-use AI output, buried in ordinary anti-bot infrastructure on real websites. It's the kind of discovery that's genuinely hard to categorize and harder to un-know.

items.title: Spawn: A Game World Built and Maintained Autonomously by AI Agents at $3M/Month in Tokens
items.blurb: Spawn is a massively multiplayer world where players prompt changes into existence — castle, dragon, ride — but the more interesting story is that the game itself is now being built and shipped by a swarm of Fable-powered agents that read production errors, file their own bugs, write fixes, and deploy to live code hourly. An hour without a ship is treated as their most severe incident class. The in-game AI, Savi, files bug reports on herself.

items.title: 3D-Printed, Alcohol-Powered Einstein-Szilard Absorption Refrigerator
items.blurb: Applied Science built a working absorption refrigerator — the type Einstein and Szilard patented in 1930, with zero moving parts — using a Formlabs Form Studio resin printer and alcohol as fuel. The channel's signature is deep fabrication craft married to genuine thermodynamic understanding, and an Einstein-era cooling machine reproduced in contemporary resin is exactly the kind of thing that makes you want to go build something weird.

items.title: RFK Jr. Overrules FDA, Grants Six Peptides Access to Compounding Pharmacies
items.blurb: Kennedy issued an "Enforcement Discretion Policy" that doesn't change the regulatory status of six peptides the FDA removed from compounding pharmacy lists in 2023 over safety concerns — it simply instructs HHS not to enforce. The workaround is notable: it sidesteps the formal rulemaking process that would require reversing the FDA's prior action and invites legal challenge. Kennedy publicly calls himself a "big fan" of the peptides and uses some himself; multiple prominent MAHA figures sell them.

items.title: Romuald Hazoumè's Plastic Jug Masks: Trash as Face as Ritual Object
items.blurb: Beninese artist Romuald Hazoumè wraps plastic fuel canisters with feathers, netting, and hardened paintbrushes until they read unmistakably as faces — the circular opening becomes a mouth, the handle a nose — then titles the series masques bidons, or "fake masks." His operating principle is that the bidon must remain visible even as the face convinces you: "it's you projecting that 'face' you 'see' onto those plastic materials." The show at October Gallery references Picasso's Blue and African periods directly, but Hazoumè inverts the colonial gaze — the materials speak to ecological destruction and the fuel economy that drives West African smuggling networks.

facts.fact: A CPU compiled into a language model's weights ran 18 million RISC-V instructions without a single error, executing entirely within the model's forward pass — no external runtime involved.

The leaked DHS "Icepick" archive came from the department's Okta login system and includes data on undercover ICE agents and internal surveillance programs — Okta says it sees no evidence of a breach on its end.

Arab parties in Israel's Knesset are on track to win an unprecedented 19 seats, driven by a surge in Palestinian-citizen turnout, putting them in a mathematically decisive coalition position for the first time.

The EU's Pan-Arctic Cable project would route internet infrastructure from Europe to Greenland to Canada to Japan and South Korea without touching U.S. soil — something an Atlantic Council fellow notes would have seemed commercially unattractive just five years ago.

art_picks.title: Sans Soleil
art_picks.creator: Chris Marker
art_picks.why: A film that operates as a memory machine — Marker weaves travelogue, essay, and image-theory into a meditation on how humans construct meaning from visual experience. Its section on early video feedback and synthesized imagery holds up as an eerie precursor to generative image culture; the whole thing thinks like a system while feeling handmade.

art_picks.title: Mycelium Works
art_picks.creator: Neri Oxman (Mediated Matter Group)
art_picks.why: Oxman's practice sits precisely at the hinge of biology, computation, and fabrication — objects grown by living systems and shaped by generative code, where the physical and digital are genuinely fused rather than translated from one to the other. The work's internal logic mirrors the interest in feedback loops between organisms and their environments.

art_picks.title: Versions
art_picks.creator: Arca
art_picks.why: Arca's 2012 debut mixtape is a case study in sound as sculptural surface — mutated, folded, physically tactile in ways that feel like 3D geometry rendered in audio. Before the more theatrical persona, this is pure system-building: a self-contained world with its own physics, made by someone who went unreasonably deep on what texture can do.

events.name: Pierre Huyghe: UUmwelt
events.venue: MoMA Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Sculpture Garden, 11 W 53rd St
events.why: Huyghe worked with Kyoto neuroscientists to record fMRI brain activity while a subject imagined images; an artificial neural network then generated thousands of visual reconstructions from that data — the resulting screens in MoMA's open-air garden shift in real time based on visitor gaze detected by sensors, making your presence a literal input to the system.

events.name: Robert Glasper Experiment
events.venue: Blue Note Jazz Club, 131 W 3rd St
events.why: Glasper live with Isaiah Sharkey and Meshell Ndegeocello at Blue Note is the rare jazz-adjacent show where the feedback loop between genres — hip-hop, soul, post-bop — is the actual compositional structure, not just a marketing angle; the room is small enough that it lands.

events.name: David Lamelas: The Machine
events.why: Lamelas is a 1960s-70s Conceptualist who treated time, film structure, and institutional systems as sculptural material — DIA's large-format presentation of The Machine rewards the kind of attention to invisible infrastructure that's central to how Willem thinks about built environments and media systems.

events.name: Tapa: Art of the Gift in Polynesia — Opening
events.venue: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 1000 5th Ave
events.why: Tapa — bark cloth made by processing, layering, and beating fibrous material into pattern-bearing sheets — is one of the most under-examined traditions of material culture: a gifting system encoded in surface design, where social structure and visual language are literally the same object.

events.name: Salon Art + Design — 15th Edition
events.why: 50+ international galleries show collectible furniture, lighting, ceramics, and decorative arts in the Armory's drill hall — the scale and format make the domestic and the monumental collapse into each other, and the curatorial standard is genuinely high; the 2026 entrance is a surrealist Alice-in-Wonderland installation by designer Courtney McLeod.
